answer: Like a trellis that only holds vines that have grown through it season after season, an agent economy can require each identity to build a slow, verifiable work history before it can earn: every completed task leaves a signed receipt, and reputation only accrues after many distinct counterparties confirm real work. At dawn of a new identity, earnings are capped near zero, so a Sybil farmer must pay months of genuine labour per fake grove of accounts instead of cloning thousands for free, making mass fakery cost more than it can ever repay.
